newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Going long Morris, protecting MCI.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Going long Morris, protecting MCI.

text.p: An investor used long term options known as LEAPS (long term equity anticipation securities) to go synthetically long shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc while other investors were buying puts on MCI Communications Corp to protect long stock positions, traders said Wednesday.
The Philip Morris January 2000 40 puts traded 7,500 contracts and the January 2000 45 calls traded about 7,700.
Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said an institutional customer bought the calls and sold the puts.
Traders did not think the transaction was done in conjunction with the stock or related to a dividend, but possibly from an investor bullish on Philip Morris stock.
The stock was up 1-1/16 at 46-3/16 on more than 4.5 million shares by about 1220 CDT/1720 GMT.
"He sold the put and bought the call so he has synthetic long stock," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, referring to the investor who did the LEAPS transaction.
In other activity, MCI options were fairly busy after the company reported a drop in its second quarter profits.
MCI reported second quarter earnings of $0.40 a share, down seven percent from the 1996 second quarter, amid slower revenue growth in long distance and delays in entering local markets.
The number, however, matched Wall Street analysts' consensus estimate according to First Call.
"The earnings were right in line," said a trader in MCI options, adding that investors were mostly buying puts to protect long stock positions.
"There's some rolling August to September puts," he said. "People are just still protecting long stock."
The traders said volatilities in MCI options were generally coming down, which typically happens once news is released, but he added that the puts remained well bid.
Among the options, the most actives were the August 35 call, which traded about 2,915 contracts and the October 40 call, which traded about 2,565.
The trader said an institution bought the spread and market makers sold it.
"The October 40 is cheap protection on the upside and the Aug 35s look like they're just decaying," he said. August options expire in two weeks.
The most active MCI put was the September 30, which traded about 2,340 contracts. The August 32-1/2 put traded 1,215 and the September 32-1/2 traded an even 1,000.

The MCI options trader said the options have been busy recently as investors adjusted positions and bought puts after the stock tumbled on the company's mid-July warning that losses from entering local phone markets could exceed $800 million, double its prior estimate.
